name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention (domain=save, descriptor=crypt_buffer) and accurately reflects the purpose: an in-place XOR cipher applied to the FD2.SAV buffer. No address residue in the name. Confirmed by callers fd2_save_current_state_to_slot / fd2_load_state_from_selected_slot using it for both encrypt and decrypt.
purpose: In-place self-inverse XOR cipher for the FD2.SAV buffer; the identical call encrypts on the write path and decrypts on the read path.
logic_summary: scramble_state = 0xA5. do { scramble_state = ROL16(scramble_state + 0x9014, 3); *pBuf ^= (byte)scramble_state; pBuf++; len--; } while (len != 0). 16-bit keystream is deterministic from the constant seed, so XOR (self-inverse) makes encrypt and decrypt the same routine. Asm uses LODSB/STOSB with ESI==EDI (true in-place) and LOOP on ECX, i.e. a do-while; len==0 underflows so callers must pass len>=1. All call sites pass length 0x59CB (full SAV image size).

params.name: pBuf
params.semantics: Base pointer of the buffer to transform in place; both source (LODSB/ESI) and destination (STOSB/EDI) point at it.
params.reason: Descriptive of the buffer pointer; no address residue. (Source models it as uint32 buf with a local uint8 *pBuf; semantically identical.)

params.name: len
params.semantics: Number of bytes to process; loop counter (ECX) decremented per byte until zero (do-while, so must be >= 1).
params.reason: Descriptive byte-count name; no address residue. (Source names it size; semantically identical.)

returns.semantics: No return value; buffer is mutated in place.
